{{Short description|None}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2021}}
{{2020 Summer Olympics}}
This is a chronological summary of the major events of the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]], which was postponed to 2021 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. The first matches in the group stages of the [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics|football]] and [[Softball at the 2020 Summer Olympics|softball]] events was held on 21 July. The opening ceremony was scheduled two days later on 23 July. The last day of competition and the closing ceremony was on 8 August.<ref name=IOC_2021_Dates>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympic.org/news/ioc-ipc-tokyo-2020-organising-committee-and-tokyo-metropolitan-government-announce-new-dates-for-the-olympic-and-paralympic-games-tokyo-2020 |title=IOC, IPC, Tokyo 2020 Organising Committee and Tokyo Metropolitan Government Announce New Dates for the Olympic and Paralympic Games Tokyo 2020 |date=30 March 2020 |website=olympic.org |publisher=[[IOC]] |access-date=30 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200330121555/https://www.olympic.org/news/ioc-ipc-tokyo-2020-organising-committee-and-tokyo-metropolitan-government-announce-new-dates-for-the-olympic-and-paralympic-games-tokyo-2020 |archive-date=30 March 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, the Games was referred to by its original date in all scheduled events in order to avoid confusion in future years.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maese |first1=Rick |title=The Olympics Are Finally Here. Here's a Guide to Help You Watch the Tokyo Summer Games. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/olympics/2021/07/22/tokyo-olympics-2021-guide/ |access-date=9 February 2022 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=23 July 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Specter |first1=Emma |title=The Tokyo Olympics Have Officially Been Rescheduled |url=https://www.vogue.com/article/2020-olympics-tokyo-rescheduled-date |access-date=9 February 2022 |work=Vogue |date=30 March 2020}}</ref> With the area under a state of emergency because of the pandemic, the Games were held largely [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] with no spectators permitted.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Tokyo Olympic Games: Spectators barred as state of emergency announced|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-57760883|access-date=July 8, 2021}}</ref>

The games featured 339 events in 33 different sports, encompassing a total of 50 disciplines. The 2020 Games saw the introduction of new competitions including [[3x3 basketball]], [[freestyle BMX]], and [[Madison (cycling)|madison cycling]], in the latter case for women (the men's version was held between 2000 and 2008 before returning in these games), as well as further mixed events. These Games also saw [[Karate at the 2020 Summer Olympics|karate]], [[Sport climbing at the 2020 Summer Olympics|sport climbing]], [[Surfing at the 2020 Summer Olympics|surfing]], and [[Skateboarding at the 2020 Summer Olympics|skateboarding]] make their Olympic debuts, as well as the return of [[Baseball at the 2020 Summer Olympics|baseball]] and [[Softball at the 2020 Summer Olympics|softball]] for the first time since [[2008 Summer Olympics|2008]].<ref name="Japan Through the Lens of the Tokyo Olympics">{{Cite book |last=Kremers |first=Daniel |title=Japan Through the Lens of the Tokyo Olympics |date=2020 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-003-03390-5 |editor=Barbara Holthus |editor2=Isaac Gagné |editor3=Wolfram Manzenreiter |editor4=Franz Waldenberger |language=en |chapter=Outdoor sports in the periphery: Far from the compact games |doi=10.4324/9781003033905 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

About 206 teams were expected to participate. This was the first Olympics since the June 2018 signing of the [[Prespa agreement]] between [[Greece]] and the Republic of Macedonia over the [[Macedonia naming dispute|"Macedonia" naming dispute]], resulting in the latter officially being renamed [[North Macedonia at the 2020 Summer Olympics|North Macedonia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1077274/ioc-approve-name-change-to-north-macedonia-national-olympic-committee|title=IOC approve name change to North Macedonia National Olympic Committee|last=Mackay|first=Duncan|date=27 March 2019|website=insidethegames.biz|access-date=4 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709163930/https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1077274/ioc-approve-name-change-to-north-macedonia-national-olympic-committee|archive-date=9 July 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> This was also the second consecutive Summer Olympics that selected independent Olympic participants to compete under the [[Olympic Flag]] as part of the "[[Refugee Olympic Team at the 2020 Summer Olympics|Refugee Olympic Team]]".<ref>{{cite web |title=29 refugee athletes to send a message of solidarity and hope to the world at the Olympic Games Tokyo 2020 |url=https://olympics.com/ioc/news/29-refugee-athletes-to-send-a-message-of-solidarity-and-hope-to-the-world-at-the-olympic-games-tokyo-2020 |access-date=8 June 2021}}</ref> As a result of the 2020 ruling by the [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] on the [[Russian doping scandal]], Russian athletes competed under the acronym "[[Russian Olympic Committee athletes at the 2020 Summer Olympics|ROC]]" after the name of the [[Russian Olympic Committee]], and under the flag of the Russian Olympic Committee.<ref>{{cite news |title=Olympics: Russia to compete under ROC acronym in Tokyo as part of doping sanctions |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-olympics-2020-russia/olympics-russia-to-compete-under-roc-acronym-in-tokyo-as-part-of-doping-sanctions-idUSKBN2AJ1UZ |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=Reuters |agency=Reuters |date=19 February 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

==Calendar==
<section begin="Calendar"/>The 2020 schedule by session was approved by the IOC Executive Board on 18&nbsp;July 2018, with the exception of swimming, diving, and artistic swimming. A more detailed schedule by event was released on 16&nbsp;April 2019, still omitting a detailed schedule for the boxing events.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tokyo2020.org/en/news/notice/20180718-01.html |title=Tokyo 2020 Unveils Action-Packed Olympic Competition Schedule |date=18 July 2018 |website=Tokyo2020 |publisher=[[Tokyo Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games|TOCOG]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180811033129/https://tokyo2020.org/en/news/notice/20180718-01.html |archive-date=11 August 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://tokyo2020.org/en/games/sport/olympic-schedule/ |title=Olympic Competition Schedule |website=Tokyo2020 |publisher=[[Tokyo Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games|TOCOG]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180720165902/https://tokyo2020.org/en/games/sport/olympic-schedule/ |archive-date=20 July 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref> A detailed boxing schedule was released in late 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tokyo2020.org/en/schedule/boxing-schedule#20200806_BOX |title=Boxing Competition Schedule |access-date=1 March 2020 |website=Tokyo2020 |publisher=[[Tokyo Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games|TOCOG]] 
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200301135613/https://tokyo2020.org/en/schedule/boxing-schedule |archive-date=1 March 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The original schedule was from 22&nbsp;July to 9&nbsp;August 2020. To postpone the Olympics until 2021, all events were delayed by 364&nbsp;days (one day less than a full year to preserve the same days of the week), giving a new schedule of 21&nbsp;July to 8&nbsp;August 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tokyo Olympics to start in July 2021 after coronavirus rescheduling |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2020/mar/30/tokyo-olympics-to-start-in-july-2021-after-coronavirus-rescheduling |website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=30 March 2020 |date=30 March 2020}}</ref>

:''All times and dates use [[Japan Standard Time]] ([[UTC+9]])''

==Day-by-day summaries==
===21 July===
;[[File:Football pictogram.svg|30px|alt=|link=]] [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics|Football]]
* The first matches in the group stage of the [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|women's tournament]] were played.<ref name=d-2>{{cite web |url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/en/results/all-sports/olympic-schedule-and-results-date=2021-07-21.htm |title=Olympic Schedule & Results - 21 Jul |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=21 July 2021 |website=Olympics.com |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=26 July 2021}}</ref>

;[[File:Softball pictogram.svg|30px|alt=|link=]] [[Softball at the 2020 Summer Olympics|Softball]]
* Group stage begins.<ref name=d-2 />

===22 July===
;[[File:Football pictogram.svg|30px|alt=|link=]] [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics|Football]]
* The first matches in the group stage of the [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Men's tournament]] were played.<ref name=d-1>{{cite web |url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/en/results/all-sports/olympic-schedule-and-results-date=2021-07-22.htm |title=Olympic Schedule & Results - 22 Jul |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=22 July 2021 |website=Olympics.com |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=26 July 2021}}</ref>

;[[File:Softball pictogram.svg|30px|alt=|link=]] [[Softball at the 2020 Summer Olympics|Softball]]
* Second day of the group stages.<ref name=d-1 />

===23 July===
;[[File:Archery pictogram.svg|30px|alt=|link=]] [[Archery at the 2020 Summer Olympics|Archery]]
* The ranking round in both the [[Archery at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's individual|men's individual competition]] and the [[Archery at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's individual|women's individual competition]] took place.<ref name=d0>{{cite web |url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/en/results/all-sports/olympic-schedule-and-results-date=2021-07-23.htm |title=Olympic Schedule & Results - 23 Jul |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=23 July 2021 |website=Olympics.com |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=26 July 2021}}</ref>

;[[File:Rowing pictogram.svg|30px|alt=|link=]] [[Rowing at the 2020 Summer Olympics|Rowing]]
* The heats in the [[Rowing at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's single sculls|men's single sculls]], [[Rowing at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's single sculls|women's single sculls]], [[Rowing at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's double sculls|men's double sculls]], [[Rowing at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's double sculls|women's double sculls]], [[Rowing at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's quadruple sculls|men's quadruple sculls]] and [[Rowing at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's quadruple sculls|women's quadruple sculls]] took place.<ref name=d0/>

;[[File:Olympic Rings Icon.svg|30px|alt=|link=]] [[2020 Summer Olympics opening ceremony|Opening ceremony]]
* The opening ceremony was held at [[Japan National Stadium]] at 20:00 [[Japan Standard Time|JST]] ([[UTC+9]]).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/en/news/naomi-osaka-lights-the-olympic-cauldron-as-tokyo-2020-gets-underway |title=Naomi Osaka lights the Olympic Cauldron as Tokyo 2020 gets underway after symbolic Opening Ceremony |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=24 July 2021 |website=Olympics.com |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=29 July 2021 |archive-date=23 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210723165116/https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/en/news/naomi-osaka-lights-the-olympic-cauldron-as-tokyo-2020-gets-underway |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Day 16: 8 August===
;[[File:Olympic Rings Icon.svg|30px|alt=|link=]] [[2020 Summer Olympics closing ceremony|Closing ceremony]]
* At [[Japan National Stadium]]. It included the traditional [[Olympic flag]] handover to [[Paris]], [[France]], the host city of the [[2024 Summer Olympics|next Summer Olympics]] in 2024.
